newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AMP sees little strategic sense in bank merger.
newsitem.headline: AMP sees little strategic sense in bank merger.

text.p: Australian Mutual Provident Society (AMP) said on Wednesday a merger with a major Australian bank after the end of the "six pillars" policy would not make strategic sense.

"We have difficulty seeing where either an acquisition by AMP or a merger with one of the four major banks makes strategic sense for AMP," AMP managing director George Trumbull said on Australian Broadcasting Commission radio.
Trumbull also said it was unlikely to make much difference to AMP if its major competitor in Australia, National Mutual Holdings Ltd, linked up with a bank.

His comments follow the government's decision to end the "six pillars" policy, which prevented mergers among the country's four biggest banks and two biggest life offices, after the release of the Wallis inquiry into the financial sector.
Trumbull said AMP, which was beaten last month in its A$4 billion bid for Scottish Amicable Life Assurance Society in Britain, would continue to look for acquisitions offshore.
"In a market the size of Australia, with the market share we have, we don't see being able to put much capital to work in Australia," he said.
"So that directs us to other major English-speaking countries which are open to us, which would be primarily the United Kingdom and the United States."
Treasurer Peter Costello also announced an end to a blanket ban on foreign takeovers of the big four banks, but Trumbull noted the large number of retail bank branches.
"I have a hard time at the current prices seeing how somebody, without significant consolidation benefits, would decide they were a good buy," he said.
